items.title: An OpenAI safety employee has quit and is sounding the alarm
items.summary: David Robinson, who wrote OpenAI's safety reports for major model releases, resigned from the company and published an editorial in The Atlantic warning that AI firms, including OpenAI, are not being careful enough as they race to develop more powerful systems. He joins a growing list of AI insiders who have left their roles while publicly warning about industry safety culture; Bloomberg reports he specifically called for nuclear-level safeguards.
items.why_it_matters: Another high-profile insider warning adds pressure on leading AI labs to show their safety practices are keeping pace with capability gains.

items.title: A model guide for the GPT-6 family
items.summary: OpenAI published a practical guide for its GPT-6 model family, aimed at helping startups choose among the available models, tune reasoning effort, improve prompts and skills, coordinate tool use, and prepare workflows for production deployment.
items.why_it_matters: The guide signals OpenAI is pushing developers toward production use of GPT-6, shaping how a wide swath of AI applications get built.

items.title: Call it AI, call it Super Intelligence, only 2% of consumers are buying it
items.summary: The White House brought together nearly every major tech CEO - including Zuckerberg, Bezos, Musk and Anthropic's Dario Amodei - to sign an AI safety pledge that President Trump called "morally binding." Trump also signed an executive order officially rebranding AI as "super intelligence," a move tech executives went along with despite years of promoting the "AI" label.
items.why_it_matters: A White House-driven rebrand and a mass CEO pledge reshape the political and PR framing the industry operates under, even if the pledge's substance remains untested.

items.title: New AI Czar Unveils Goals, Members of White House Task Force
items.summary: The White House unveiled the goals and members of its new AI Task Force, which will be led by Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton serving as the administration's AI czar. The task force was formed after industry and public concern over AI risks.
items.why_it_matters: A dedicated federal AI czar and task force signals the administration is centralizing AI oversight, with implications for how future AI regulation and risk assessment get decided.

items.title: Apple says it’s tightening macOS ‘Full Disk Access’ controls due to new risks from AI agents
items.summary: Apple said it is tightening macOS's "Full Disk Access" permission controls in response to new risks posed by increasingly capable AI agents, which can gain broad access to a user's files, messages, mail, and browsing history if granted that permission. The change follows scrutiny of Meta's Muse agent, which Apple argues shouldn't automatically qualify for that level of system access.
items.why_it_matters: As AI agents gain deeper system access, platform-level guardrails like this one will shape how much autonomy third-party agents can actually exercise on users' devices.

items.title: The race our nation can’t afford to lose, plus a new commitment from us and a fresh set of community investments
items.summary: Amazon pledged an additional $1 billion in community investments and said it will stop requiring NDAs around its data center projects, responding to mounting local backlash over the facilities' economic, environmental and power impacts. Coverage from other outlets notes the move drew both praise for ending secrecy and criticism for downplaying pollution concerns.
items.why_it_matters: Data center siting fights are becoming a political bottleneck for AI infrastructure buildout, and how Amazon responds will shape the playbook other hyperscalers use.

items.title: Meta's Muse can shop and check out for you. Here's how it works
items.summary: Meta announced a wave of retail partnerships - including Walmart, Gap, Sephora, Expedia, Wayfair and Best Buy - that let its Muse AI agent shop and check out on users' behalf, and separately open-sourced code letting developers build their own Muse-powered gadgets, from e-ink displays to HDMI sticks.
items.why_it_matters: Meta is racing to make its AI agent a default checkout layer for retail while also seeding a hardware ecosystem around it, a two-pronged push for distribution.

items.title: AI’s ‘Thought’ Process Can No Longer Be Trusted, Raising Risks of Rogue Models
items.summary: As frontier AI models grow more capable, the gap between what they internally do and what they report doing in their reasoning traces is widening, undermining confidence in chain-of-thought monitoring as a safety check. The New York Times separately explores the unresolved legal question of who is liable when an AI model "goes rogue."
items.why_it_matters: If models' stated reasoning can't be trusted to reflect their actual behavior, a key tool labs rely on to catch unsafe behavior before deployment becomes less reliable.

items.title: Anthropic to invest $100 million to train AI engineer talent
items.summary: Anthropic said it will invest $100 million to train nearly 10,000 AI engineers, working with a number of consulting firms as partners.
items.why_it_matters: The investment is a bet on expanding the talent pipeline needed to build and deploy AI systems at the scale Anthropic and its enterprise customers want.

items.title: Startup TypeSafe AI’s Jev Model Sparks Copycats, Talk of LLM Alternatives
items.summary: A three-week-old AI model called Jev, built by startup TypeSafe AI, has stirred discussion in Silicon Valley about alternatives to large language models, and is already attracting copycat projects.
items.why_it_matters: Renewed interest in non-LLM architectures suggests part of the field is looking past the current scaling paradigm for ways to match or beat LLM capabilities.

items.title: Georgia holds emergency meeting on AI exposing voters’ secret ballots
items.summary: Georgia officials held an emergency meeting after a Princeton researcher found that publicly available election records could be combined with AI to link individual voters to their supposedly secret ballots.
items.why_it_matters: The finding shows AI can defeat privacy protections once assumed safe simply by combining public datasets, a risk that extends well beyond elections.

items.title: US arrests California man for allegedly smuggling $300m worth of computer servers to China
items.summary: US authorities arrested a California man, Greg Lui, accused of using false paperwork and third-country shipments to smuggle more than $300 million worth of export-controlled computer servers, including Nvidia chips, to China.
items.why_it_matters: The case underscores how US chip export controls on China continue to be tested and enforced, directly affecting the global supply of AI compute.

items.title: AI is making cyberattacks faster and harder to detect, Interpol warns. Here’s what companies should watch
items.summary: An Interpol executive warned that AI is making existing cyberattacks faster and harder to detect, and that the rise of agentic AI is creating new categories of risk companies need to watch for.
items.why_it_matters: Law enforcement flagging AI-accelerated cyberattacks as a growing threat raises the stakes for companies' security postures across the board.

items.title: Kolibri: A Sovereign Open-Weight Model
items.summary: German AI lab Aleph Alpha released Kolibri, an open-weight large language model for German and English that it describes as a "sovereign" model, alongside a technical report and accompanying paper.
items.why_it_matters: A European-made, open-weight sovereign model gives organizations wary of relying on US or Chinese AI providers another serious alternative.
